hens_rule_text: Up to 6 hens for non-commercial, personal use on residential property; no roosters.
permit_notes: Search extracts describe periodic inspection of chicken housing by a city inspector but did not confirm whether a permit or registration is required before keeping hens.
setback_notes: Search extracts report coops or chicken housing must be kept at least 25 ft from property lines; whether this is measured from a neighbor's dwelling specifically was not confirmed.
coop_rules: Chickens must be confined and may not run at large on streets, parks or other public property; poultry yards and enclosures must be kept clean and sanitary and free of refuse.
zoning_notes: Rules found in City Code Chapter 6, Animals and Fowl, apply city-wide to residential keeping since a 2015 city council amendment; not confirmed by zoning district.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: Newport News, VA Code of Ordinances, Chapter 6 Animals and Fowl (Municode)
Peninsula Chicken Keepers (PeCK): Newport News local law brochure (2015 city council amendment)

research_notes: Facts (6-hen cap, no roosters, 25 ft setback, no on-site slaughter, general poultry-at-large and sanitation rules) come from a WebSearch extract of the Municode Chapter 6 page and a secondary local advocacy group brochure describing the 2015 ordinance change; Municode itself is region-blocked from this machine and was not opened directly, and whether a permit is required was not established.
